chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Abu Waddad, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who takes an animal or a camel as a pledge for his money, whether he has the right to ride it. He said: 'If he feeds it, he has the right to ride it; and if the one who pledged it to him feeds it, he does not have the right to ride it.'
ai.seo_question: Can a creditor ride the animal pledged as collateral for a debt?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *qabd* (possession) and *nafqa* (maintenance) in Islamic pledge law, where the right to usufruct is contingent upon bearing the cost of upkeep. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on fairness in commercial transactions, ensuring that the pledgee does not unjustly benefit from the asset if the pledger retains the financial burden of its care. This ruling is foundational in *Fiqh al-Rahin* and highlights the practical application of equity in debt recovery mechanisms.
